locators: p. 1, General Instructions, "Use Schedule B (Form 1040) if any of the following applies", "You received interest from a seller-financed mortgage", "You have accrued interest from a bond", "You are reporting original issue discount (OID) of less than the amount shown on Form 1099-OID", "You are reporting interest income of less than the amount shown on a Form 1099 due to amortizable bond premium", "You are claiming the exclusion of interest from series EE or I U.S. savings bonds issued after 1989", "You received interest or ordinary dividends as a nominee"
pp. 1–3, interest, dividends and foreign accounts/trusts

findings.who: A filer whose only Form 1099-INT or 1099-DIV is for an account held in their name for a parent or child, or as a nominee for someone else. They passed every dollar on to the actual owner.
findings.why_no: The helper asks for 'Taxable interest' and 'ordinary dividends'. The money was never theirs and was not taxable to them, so they enter $0, even though the helper says 'before any Schedule B adjustment'. The gate is false, so the nominee question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1: 'If you received a Form 1099-INT that includes interest you received as a nominee ... report the total on line 1. Do this even if you later distributed some or all of this income to others.' p. 2 gives the same rule for Form 1099-DIV on line 5.
findings.fix: Gate on the forms and amounts, not on 'taxable' income: 'Did you or your spouse get any Form 1099-INT, 1099-OID or 1099-DIV, or substitute statement, even if some or all of it belongs to someone else?' Add to the helper: 'include amounts you received for someone else.'

findings.who: A filer who sold a house with seller financing, and the buyer lives in it. The buyer pays monthly, the filer gets no Form 1099-INT, and they have no bank interest.
findings.why_no: 'Taxable interest from all payers' reads as interest shown on 1099s from banks. They see the buyer's payments as installments on a sale, not as interest from a 'payer', and enter $0.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1: 'If you sold your home or other property and the buyer used the property as a personal residence, list first any interest the buyer paid you on a mortgage or other form of seller financing. Be sure to show the buyer's name, address, and SSN.'
findings.fix: Ask about the fact separately, outside the gate: 'Did you or your spouse sell property and finance any of the price yourself (the buyer pays you over time)?' Count a yes as interest for the gate.

findings.who: A filer who cashed series EE or I bonds issued after 1989 and paid qualified tuition that year. All of the interest is excludable, and they have no other interest.
findings.why_no: They read 'Taxable interest' as the interest after the education exclusion, which is $0. 'Before any Schedule B adjustment' does not say that the savings bond exclusion is such an adjustment.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1: 'Include interest from series EE, H, HH, and I U.S. savings bonds.' p. 2, Line 3: 'If, during 2025, you cashed series EE or I U.S. savings bonds issued after 1989 and you paid qualified higher education expenses ... you may be able to exclude part or all of the interest.'
findings.fix: Helper text: 'All interest shown on Forms 1099-INT and 1099-OID or received without a form, including savings bond interest you expect to exclude, interest you will reduce for bond premium, OID or accrued interest, and interest belonging to someone else.'

findings.who: A filer who holds only municipal bonds bought at a market discount, or who sold one. Or a filer whose only bond is a contingent payment debt instrument that was sold at a gain, or one held only through Form 1099-OID.
findings.why_no: All of their bond income feels 'tax-exempt', or it shows up as a sale gain or as OID, not as 'interest'. So taxable interest is $0 to them, and the special items are never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1: 'Also include any accrued market discount that is includible in income and any gain on a contingent payment debt instrument that is includible in income as interest income.' Also: 'The market discount on a tax-exempt bond is taxable interest income and not tax-exempt interest.'
findings.fix: Widen the gate: 'Did you or your spouse own, buy or sell any bond, note or other debt instrument, including tax-exempt bonds, or get any Form 1099-INT, 1099-OID or 1099-DIV?' Then ask about the special items.

findings.who: A married couple filing jointly. Only the spouse has a savings account or a bond with a Form 1099-INT, or nominee interest.
findings.why_no: The interest helper says 'Taxable interest from all payers' without 'you or your spouse', while the dividend helpers say it. The filer counts only their own interest.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1: 'Report on line 1 all of your taxable interest.' On a joint return, this covers both spouses.
findings.fix: Reword the helper to 'Taxable interest you or your spouse received from all payers, before any Schedule B adjustment.'

findings.who: A filer with no interest or dividends who has signature authority over an employer's foreign bank account. Or one who received a distribution, or a cash loan, from a foreign trust, or was a grantor of or transferor to one.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed only from interest, dividends and capital gain distributions, all $0. The input cites the foreign accounts/trusts pages, but nothing about the foreign account or trust is asked under this gate.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1: 'Use Schedule B (Form 1040) if any of the following applies. ... You had a financial interest in, or signature authority over, a financial account in a foreign country or you received a distribution from, or were a grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust.'
findings.fix: Unless Part III is gated separately and not by income, add to the gate a computed or asked condition: 'At any time in 2025, did you or your spouse have a financial interest in or signature authority over a foreign financial account, or receive a distribution or loan from, or create or transfer property to, a foreign trust?'

findings.who: A filer whose only dividends come with no Form 1099-DIV. Examples are a small dividend from a foreign corporation held directly, or dividends shown only on a substitute statement or a K-1, and some of them belong to someone else.
findings.why_no: The dividend helper says 'Form 1099-DIV box 1a', so with no 1099-DIV they enter $0.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2: 'Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends. This amount should be shown in box 1a of your Forms 1099-DIV or substitute statements.'
findings.fix: Helper text: 'Ordinary dividends you or your spouse received, from Form 1099-DIV box 1a, substitute statements, or with no form.'
